docs.title: Mydia
docs.text:
Your personal media companion, built with Phoenix LiveView

A modern, self-hosted media management platform for tracking, organizing, and monitoring your media library.

Early Development

Mydia is still in version 0.x.x and is subject to major changes from version to version. Feedback is welcome! Expect bugs and please open issues or feature requests.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Unified Media Management - Track both movies and TV shows with rich metadata from TMDB/TVDB
  • Automated Downloads - Background search and download with quality profiles and smart release ranking
  • Download Clients - qBittorrent, Transmission, SABnzbd, and NZBGet support
  • Indexer Integration - Search via Prowlarr and Jackett for finding releases
  • Built-in Indexer Library - Native Cardigann support (experimental, limited testing)
  • Multi-User System - Built-in admin/guest roles with request approval workflow
  • SSO Support - Local authentication plus OIDC/OpenID Connect integration
  • Release Calendar - Track upcoming releases and monitor episodes
  • Import Lists - Sync external lists from TMDB (watchlists, popular, trending) to auto-add content (experimental)
  • Modern Real-Time UI - Phoenix LiveView with instant updates and responsive design

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Get started with Mydia in minutes using Docker Compose:

services:
  mydia:
    image: ghcr.io/getmydia/mydia:latest
    container_name: mydia
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - SECRET_KEY_BASE=your-secret-key-base-here
      - GUARDIAN_SECRET_KEY=your-guardian-secret-key-here
      - PHX_HOST=localhost
      - PORT=4000
      - MOVIES_PATH=/media/library/movies
      - TV_PATH=/media/library/tv
    volumes:
      - /path/to/mydia/config:/config
      - /path/to/your/media:/media
    ports:
      - 4000:4000
    restart: unless-stopped

Generate the required secrets:

# Generate SECRET_KEY_BASE
openssl rand -base64 48

# Generate GUARDIAN_SECRET_KEY
openssl rand -base64 48

For detailed setup instructions, see the Getting Started Guide.

docs.title: Cardigann Indexers
docs.text:
Mydia includes built-in Cardigann indexer support, allowing direct indexer connections without Prowlarr or Jackett.

Experimental Feature

Cardigann support is highly experimental. Only a limited number of indexers have been tested. If you encounter issues, please report them on GitHub.

docs.title: What is Cardigann?
docs.text:
Cardigann is a generic indexer definition format that describes how to interact with torrent/usenet indexers. It was originally developed for Jackett and is now used by Prowlarr as well.

Mydia includes a native Cardigann implementation, allowing you to use hundreds of indexers directly without running a separate indexer manager.

docs.title: Enabling Cardigann
docs.text:
Cardigann is enabled by default:

ENABLE_CARDIGANN=true

To disable:

ENABLE_CARDIGANN=false

docs.title: Supported Indexers
docs.text:
Mydia includes definitions for many popular indexers. However, only a subset have been thoroughly tested.

Tested Indexers:

  • 1337x
  • RARBG (mirrors)
  • YTS
  • And others...

Untested but Included:

Many more indexer definitions are included but haven't been verified. They may work, have issues, or not work at all.

docs.title: Adding a Cardigann Indexer
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Admin > Indexers
  2. Click Add Indexer
  3. Select the indexer from the Cardigann list
  4. Enter required credentials (if applicable)
  5. Test and save

docs.title: Indexer Settings
docs.text:
Each indexer may have specific settings:

  • Username/Password
  • API Key
  • Cookie authentication
  • Site-specific options

Refer to the indexer's requirements in the Admin UI.

docs.title: Known Issues
docs.text:
• Some indexers may not parse results correctly
  • Authentication may fail on some sites
  • Rate limiting varies by indexer
  • CAPTCHA challenges not supported

docs.title: When to Use Prowlarr/Jackett
docs.text:
Consider using Prowlarr or Jackett instead if:

  • You need more reliable indexer support
  • You require specific indexers that don't work with Cardigann
  • You want centralized indexer management
  • You need advanced features like sync

docs.title: Search Returns No Results
docs.text:
1. Test the indexer connection
  2. Check if the site is accessible
  3. Verify credentials if required
  4. Check application logs for errors

docs.title: Authentication Errors
docs.text:
1. Verify credentials are correct
  2. Some sites require manual cookie refresh
  3. Check if site requires 2FA (not supported)

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
1. Reduce search frequency
  2. Add delay between requests
  3. Consider using fewer indexers

docs.title: Reporting Issues
docs.text:
When reporting Cardigann issues:

  1. Include the indexer name
  2. Describe the expected vs. actual behavior
  3. Include relevant log entries
  4. Specify if it works with Prowlarr/Jackett

docs.text:

docs.text:
# flake.nix
{
  inputs.mydia.url = "github:getmydia/mydia";

  outputs = { self, nixpkgs, mydia }: {
    nixosConfigurations.myserver = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem {
      modules = [ mydia.nixosModules.default ./configuration.nix ];
    };
  };
}

{
  services.mydia = {
    enable = true;

    secretKeyBaseFile = "/run/secrets/mydia/secret_key_base";
    guardianSecretKeyFile = "/run/secrets/mydia/guardian_secret_key";
    mediaLibraries = [ "/mnt/media/movies" "/mnt/media/tv" ];

docs.title: SSO/OIDC Configuration
docs.text: Mydia supports OpenID Connect (OIDC) for single sign-on integration.

docs.title: Supported Providers
docs.text:
Mydia works with any OIDC-compliant provider:

  • Keycloak
  • Authelia
  • Auth0
  • Okta
  • Azure AD
  • Google
  • And more...

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
OIDC_ENABLED=true
OIDC_DISCOVERY_DOCUMENT_URI=https://your-provider/.well-known/openid-configuration
OIDC_CLIENT_ID=mydia
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
OIDC_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:4000/auth/oidc/callback
OIDC_SCOPES=openid profile email

docs.title: Variable Reference
docs.text: Variable Description Required OIDC_ENABLED Enable OIDC authentication Yes OIDC_DISCOVERY_DOCUMENT_URI Provider's discovery endpoint Yes OIDC_CLIENT_ID Application client ID Yes OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET Application client secret Yes OIDC_REDIRECT_URI Callback URL (auto-computed if not set) No OIDC_SCOPES Space-separated scope list No

docs.title: Minimal Configuration
docs.text:
Mydia uses standard OAuth2 authentication. Configure your provider with:

  1. Client ID - Unique identifier for Mydia
  2. Client Secret - Secret key for authentication
  3. Redirect URI - https://your-mydia-host/auth/oidc/callback

No need to configure:

  • Token endpoint auth methods
  • Response modes
  • JWT-based authentication
  • PAR settings

docs.title: Keycloak Example
docs.text:
1. Create a new client in your realm
  2. Set client protocol to openid-connect
  3. Set access type to confidential
  4. Add redirect URI: https://mydia.example.com/auth/oidc/callback
  5. Copy client ID and secret
OIDC_DISCOVERY_DOCUMENT_URI=https://keycloak.example.com/realms/myrealm/.well-known/openid-configuration
OIDC_CLIENT_ID=mydia
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret

docs.title: Authelia Example
docs.text:
1. Add client configuration to Authelia:
identity_providers:
  oidc:
    clients:
      - client_id: mydia
        client_secret: your-client-secret
        redirect_uris:
          - https://mydia.example.com/auth/oidc/callback
        scopes:
          - openid
          - profile
          - email
  1. Configure Mydia:
OIDC_DISCOVERY_DOCUMENT_URI=https://authelia.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration
OIDC_CLIENT_ID=mydia
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret

docs.title: Auth0 Example
docs.text:
1. Create a new Regular Web Application
  2. Configure allowed callback URLs
  3. Copy domain, client ID, and secret
OIDC_DISCOVERY_DOCUMENT_URI=https://your-tenant.auth0.com/.well-known/openid-configuration
OIDC_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret

docs.title: Google Example
docs.text:
1. Create OAuth 2.0 credentials in Google Cloud Console
  2. Add authorized redirect URIs
  3. Copy client ID and secret
OIDC_DISCOVERY_DOCUMENT_URI=https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration
OIDC_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret

docs.title: First User Promotion
docs.text: The first user to log in via OIDC is automatically promoted to admin role. Subsequent users are assigned guest role.

docs.title: Role Assignment
docs.text:
Currently, role assignment is manual after first login:

  1. Admin logs in
  2. Navigates to Admin > Users
  3. Updates user role as needed

docs.title: Combining with Local Auth
docs.text:
You can use both local and OIDC authentication:

LOCAL_AUTH_ENABLED=true
OIDC_ENABLED=true

Users see options for both on the login page.

docs.title: Disabling Local Auth
docs.text:
For OIDC-only authentication:

LOCAL_AUTH_ENABLED=false
OIDC_ENABLED=true

Warning

Ensure OIDC is working before disabling local auth to avoid lockout.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text:
Default scopes:

OIDC_SCOPES=openid profile email

Required scopes:

  • openid - Required for OIDC
  • profile - User profile information
  • email - User email address

docs.title: Redirect URI
docs.text:
The redirect URI is auto-computed from your PHX_HOST and URL_SCHEME:

{URL_SCHEME}://{PHX_HOST}/auth/oidc/callback

Override with:

OIDC_REDIRECT_URI=https://mydia.example.com/auth/oidc/callback

docs.title: Login Fails
docs.text:
1. Check discovery document URI is accessible
  2. Verify client ID and secret
  3. Check redirect URI matches provider configuration
  4. Review application logs for errors

docs.title: User Not Created
docs.text:
1. Ensure required scopes are granted
  2. Check provider returns email claim
  3. Review application logs

docs.title: Session Issues
docs.text:
1. Check cookie settings
  2. Verify HTTPS configuration
  3. Check PHX_HOST matches your domain

docs.title: PostgreSQL Support
docs.text: Mydia provides separate Docker images for PostgreSQL users.

docs.title: Image Selection
docs.text:
Image Tag Database latest SQLite latest-pg PostgreSQL

Image Compatibility

The database adapter is compiled into the image. SQLite and PostgreSQL images are not interchangeable at runtime.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: mydia
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: changeme
      POSTGRES_DB: mydia
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U mydia"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  mydia:
    image: ghcr.io/getmydia/mydia:latest-pg
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      DATABASE_TYPE: postgres
      DATABASE_HOST: postgres
      DATABASE_PORT: 5432
      DATABASE_NAME: mydia
      DATABASE_USER: mydia
      DATABASE_PASSWORD: changeme
      SECRET_KEY_BASE: your-secret-key-base
      GUARDIAN_SECRET_KEY: your-guardian-secret
      PHX_HOST: localhost
      PORT: 4000
      MOVIES_PATH: /media/movies
      TV_PATH: /media/tv
    volumes:
      - ./config:/config
      - /path/to/media:/media
    ports:
      - "4000:4000"

volumes:
  postgres_data:

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Default DATABASE_TYPE Set to postgres sqlite DATABASE_HOST PostgreSQL hostname localhost DATABASE_PORT PostgreSQL port 5432 DATABASE_NAME Database name mydia DATABASE_USER Database username postgres DATABASE_PASSWORD Database password - POOL_SIZE Connection pool size 10

docs.title: Connection Pooling
docs.text:
Adjust pool size based on your workload:

POOL_SIZE=20

For high-traffic deployments, consider using PgBouncer.

docs.title: Backup
docs.text:
pg_dump -h localhost -U mydia mydia > backup.sql

Or using Docker:

docker compose exec postgres pg_dump -U mydia mydia > backup.sql

docs.title: Restore
docs.text:
psql -h localhost -U mydia mydia < backup.sql

Or using Docker:

docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U mydia mydia < backup.sql

docs.title: PostgreSQL Configuration
docs.text:
For better performance, tune PostgreSQL settings:

-- In postgresql.conf
shared_buffers = 256MB
effective_cache_size = 768MB
work_mem = 4MB
maintenance_work_mem = 64MB
wal_buffers = 8MB

docs.title: Connection Settings
docs.text:
# Increase pool for high concurrency
POOL_SIZE=30

docs.title: External PostgreSQL
docs.text:
To use an existing PostgreSQL server:

DATABASE_TYPE=postgres
DATABASE_HOST=your-postgres-server.example.com
DATABASE_PORT=5432
DATABASE_NAME=mydia
DATABASE_USER=mydia
DATABASE_PASSWORD=secure-password

Ensure:

  • Network connectivity between Mydia and PostgreSQL
  • Database and user exist
  • User has appropriate permissions

docs.title: Version Requirements
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL 12 or later recommended
  • PostgreSQL 16 tested

docs.title: Connection Refused
docs.text:
1. Verify PostgreSQL is running
  2. Check hostname and port
  3. Verify credentials
  4. Check network connectivity

docs.title: Permission Denied
docs.text:
1. Verify database user exists
  2. Check user permissions:
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE mydia TO mydia;

docs.title: Slow Queries
docs.text:
1. Check PostgreSQL logs
  2. Run ANALYZE on tables
  3. Review connection pool settings
  4. Check server resources

docs.title: When to Use PostgreSQL
docs.text:
Use PostgreSQL for:

  • High-concurrency environments
  • Existing PostgreSQL infrastructure
  • Advanced querying needs
  • Horizontal scaling requirements

Use SQLite for:

  • Personal/home use
  • Simple deployments
  • Single-user scenarios
  • Minimal resource usage

docs.title: Web Layer
docs.text:
Phoenix LiveView provides real-time updates without writing JavaScript:

  • Server-rendered HTML - Initial page load
  • WebSocket connection - Real-time updates
  • LiveComponents - Reusable stateful components

docs.title: Business Logic
docs.text:
Organized into contexts following Phoenix conventions:

  • Mydia.Libraries - Library and media management
  • Mydia.Downloads - Download client integration
  • Mydia.Indexers - Indexer search and configuration
  • Mydia.Accounts - User authentication

docs.title: Background Jobs
docs.text:
Oban handles async tasks:

  • MediaScanWorker - Scans library directories
  • DownloadMonitorWorker - Monitors download progress
  • MetadataWorker - Fetches external metadata

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text:
Ecto schemas define the data model:

  • Movie/Series - Media items
  • MediaFile - Physical files
  • Download - Download queue entries
  • QualityProfile - Quality preferences

docs.title: Metadata Relay
docs.text:
A companion service that:

  • Proxies metadata requests to TVDB/TMDB
  • Protects API keys
  • Reduces rate limiting issues

docs.title: Download Clients
docs.text:
Adapter pattern for different clients:

  • qBittorrent (HTTP API)
  • Transmission (RPC)
  • SABnzbd (HTTP API)
  • NZBGet (JSON-RPC)

docs.title: Indexers
docs.text:
Integration with:

  • Prowlarr (unified indexer management)
  • Jackett (indexer proxy)
  • Cardigann (native indexer definitions)

docs.title: LiveView Over SPA
docs.text:
Benefits:

  • Simpler development (no separate frontend)
  • Real-time by default
  • SEO-friendly
  • Reduced complexity

docs.title: SQLite Default
docs.text:
Benefits:

  • Zero configuration
  • Single-file backup
  • Sufficient for personal use
  • PostgreSQL available for scaling

docs.title: Relative Path Storage
docs.text:
Media files stored with relative paths:

  • Portable database
  • Easy library relocation
  • No path updates needed

docs.title: Oban for Jobs
docs.text:
Benefits:

  • Persistent job queue
  • Automatic retries
  • Monitoring/visibility
  • Transaction-safe

docs.title: Adding Media
docs.text:

docs.title: Complete Stack Example
docs.text:
A production-ready setup with Mydia, Transmission (torrent client), and Prowlarr (indexer manager):

services:
  # =============================================================================
  # MYDIA - Media Management
  # =============================================================================
  mydia:
    image: ghcr.io/getmydia/mydia:latest
    container_name: mydia
    environment:
      # --- Required Secrets (generate with: openssl rand -base64 48) ---
      - SECRET_KEY_BASE=your-64-character-secret-key-base-here
      - GUARDIAN_SECRET_KEY=your-64-character-guardian-secret-here

      # --- Container Settings ---
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York

      # --- Server Settings ---
      - PHX_HOST=mydia.local
      - PORT=4000
      - URL_SCHEME=http

      # --- Media Library Paths ---
      - MOVIES_PATH=/media/library/movies
      - TV_PATH=/media/library/tv

      # --- Transmission Download Client ---
      - DOWNLOAD_CLIENT_1_NAME=Transmission
      - DOWNLOAD_CLIENT_1_TYPE=transmission
      - DOWNLOAD_CLIENT_1_ENABLED=true
      - DOWNLOAD_CLIENT_1_HOST=transmission
      - DOWNLOAD_CLIENT_1_PORT=9091
      - DOWNLOAD_CLIENT_1_USERNAME=admin
      - DOWNLOAD_CLIENT_1_PASSWORD=transmission
      - DOWNLOAD_CLIENT_1_CATEGORY=mydia
      - DOWNLOAD_CLIENT_1_DOWNLOAD_DIRECTORY=/media/downloads

      # --- Prowlarr Indexer ---
      - INDEXER_1_NAME=Prowlarr
      - INDEXER_1_TYPE=prowlarr
      - INDEXER_1_ENABLED=true
      - INDEXER_1_BASE_URL=http://prowlarr:9696
      - INDEXER_1_API_KEY=your-prowlarr-api-key-here
    volumes:
      - ./config/mydia:/config
      - /path/to/media:/media
    ports:
      - "4000:4000"
    depends_on:
      - transmission
      - prowlarr
    restart: unless-stopped

  # =============================================================================
  # TRANSMISSION - Torrent Client
  # =============================================================================
  transmission:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/transmission:latest
    container_name: transmission
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - USER=admin
      - PASS=transmission
    volumes:
      - ./config/transmission:/config
      - /path/to/media/downloads:/media/downloads
    ports:
      - "9091:9091"
      - "51413:51413"
      - "51413:51413/udp"
    restart: unless-stopped

  # =============================================================================
  # PROWLARR - Indexer Manager
  # =============================================================================
  prowlarr:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/prowlarr:latest
    container_name: prowlarr
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - ./config/prowlarr:/config
    ports:
      - "9696:9696"
    restart: unless-stopped

Getting Your Prowlarr API Key

  1. Start the stack: docker compose up -d
  2. Access Prowlarr at http://localhost:9696
  3. Go to Settings → General and copy the API Key
  4. Update INDEXER_1_API_KEY in your compose file
  5. Restart Mydia: docker compose restart mydia

docs.title: Hardlink Support
docs.text:
For optimal storage efficiency, Mydia uses hardlinks when importing media. To enable hardlinks, ensure your downloads and library directories are on the same filesystem:

volumes:
  - /path/to/mydia/config:/config
  - /path/to/your/media:/media  # Single mount for downloads AND libraries

Organize your host directory structure:

/path/to/your/media/
  ├── downloads/          # Download client output
  └── library/
      ├── movies/         # Movies library
      └── tv/             # TV library

Benefits:

  • Instant file operations (no data copying)
  • Zero duplicate storage space
  • Files remain seeding while available in your library

docs.title: User/Group Identifiers
docs.text:
To avoid permission issues, specify the user PUID and group PGID:

id your_user
# Example output: uid=1000(your_user) gid=1000(your_user)

Use these values for PUID and PGID in your container configuration.

services:

      - /path/to/mydia/config:/config
      - /path/to/your/media:/media

docs.text:
Coming Soon

API documentation is planned for a future release. Mydia currently provides a web interface for all functionality.

docs.title: Current State
docs.text: Mydia does not currently expose a public REST API. All functionality is accessible through the Phoenix LiveView web interface.

docs.title: Planned Features
docs.text:
Future API support may include:

  • REST API for media management
  • WebSocket events for real-time updates
  • API key authentication
  • Rate limiting

docs.title: Internal APIs
docs.text:
Mydia uses internal APIs for:

  • Download client communication (qBittorrent, Transmission, SABnzbd, NZBGet)
  • Indexer queries (Prowlarr, Jackett)
  • Metadata fetching (via metadata-relay service)

These are implementation details and not intended for external use.

docs.title: Integration Options
docs.text:
Currently, you can integrate with Mydia through:

  1. Download Clients - Configure in Admin UI
  2. Indexers - Configure in Admin UI
  3. OIDC/SSO - Authenticate via external identity providers

docs.text: If you're interested in API development, check the Development documentation and consider contributing to the project.

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: Mydia supports multiple configuration sources with a defined precedence order.

docs.title: 1. Environment Variables (Highest Priority)
docs.text: Environment variables override all other configuration sources. See Environment Variables for complete reference.

docs.title: 2. Database Settings
docs.text:
Settings configured through the Admin UI are stored in the database and persist across restarts.

Access via Admin > Settings.

docs.title: 3. YAML Configuration File
docs.text:
Place a config.yml file in the /config directory:

# /config/config.yml
movies_path: /media/movies
tv_path: /media/tv
scan_interval_hours: 2

docs.title: 4. Schema Defaults (Lowest Priority)
docs.text: Built-in defaults are used when no other configuration is specified.

docs.title: Changing Library Paths
docs.text:
Via Environment Variables:

MOVIES_PATH=/new/path/movies
TV_PATH=/new/path/tv

Via Admin UI:

  1. Navigate to Admin > Settings
  2. Update library paths
  3. Mydia validates files are accessible before saving

docs.text:
For proper link generation:

PHX_HOST=mydia.example.com

docs.text: Database settings are included in automatic database backups. Environment variables and YAML files should be backed up separately as part of your infrastructure management.

docs.title: Database Reference
docs.text: Mydia supports SQLite (default) and PostgreSQL databases.

docs.title: SQLite (Default)
docs.text: SQLite is the default database, providing a simple single-file setup.

docs.title: Location
docs.text:
The database file is stored at:

/config/mydia.db

Configure with:

DATABASE_PATH=/config/mydia.db

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• Zero configuration
  • Single file backup
  • Perfect for personal/home use
  • No external dependencies

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Single-writer at a time
  • Not suitable for high-concurrency

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.text: For deployments requiring higher concurrency or existing PostgreSQL infrastructure.

docs.title: Image Selection
docs.text:
Use the PostgreSQL-specific image:

ghcr.io/getmydia/mydia:latest-pg

Image Selection

The database adapter is compiled into the image. SQLite and PostgreSQL images are not interchangeable.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
DATABASE_TYPE=postgres
DATABASE_HOST=postgres
DATABASE_PORT=5432
DATABASE_NAME=mydia
DATABASE_USER=mydia
DATABASE_PASSWORD=your-password
POOL_SIZE=10

docs.title: Docker Compose Example
docs.text:
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: mydia
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: changeme
      POSTGRES_DB: mydia
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U mydia"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

  mydia:
    image: ghcr.io/getmydia/mydia:latest-pg
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      DATABASE_TYPE: postgres
      DATABASE_HOST: postgres
      DATABASE_NAME: mydia
      DATABASE_USER: mydia
      DATABASE_PASSWORD: changeme
      # ... other variables

volumes:
  postgres_data:

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text: Database migrations run automatically on startup.

docs.title: Automatic Backups
docs.text:
Before running migrations, Mydia creates a backup:

  • SQLite: Backup file created alongside database
  • PostgreSQL: Recommend external backup solution

docs.title: Backup Location
docs.text:
/config/mydia_backup_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.db

Only the 10 most recent backups are kept.

docs.title: Disabling Backups
docs.text:
SKIP_BACKUPS=true

Warning

Not recommended. Manual backups should be in place.

docs.title: SQLite
docs.text:
Backup:

# Stop container first
docker compose stop mydia

# Copy database file
cp /path/to/config/mydia.db /path/to/backup/

Restore:

# Stop container
docker compose stop mydia

# Replace database file
cp /path/to/backup/mydia.db /path/to/config/

# Start container
docker compose start mydia

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.text:
Use standard PostgreSQL backup tools:

# Backup
pg_dump -U mydia mydia > backup.sql

# Restore
psql -U mydia mydia < backup.sql

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text:
Mydia uses Ecto for database management. The schema includes:

  • Users - User accounts and authentication
  • Libraries - Media library configurations
  • Movies - Movie metadata and files
  • Series - TV show metadata
  • Seasons - TV show seasons
  • Episodes - TV show episodes
  • MediaFiles - File references and metadata
  • Downloads - Download queue and history
  • Indexers - Indexer configurations
  • DownloadClients - Download client configurations
  • QualityProfiles - Quality profile definitions

docs.title: SQLite
docs.text:
SQLite performance is generally excellent for personal use. For very large libraries:

  • Ensure database is on fast storage (SSD)
  • Regular VACUUM operations (performed automatically)

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.text:
For high-performance deployments:

POOL_SIZE=20  # Increase connection pool

Configure PostgreSQL server settings:

-- In postgresql.conf
shared_buffers = 256MB
effective_cache_size = 768MB
work_mem = 4MB

docs.title: Migration from SQLite to PostgreSQL
docs.text:
Warning

No automated migration tool is provided. Manual data migration is required.

  1. Export data from SQLite
  2. Deploy PostgreSQL instance
  3. Import data to PostgreSQL
  4. Switch to latest-pg image

docs.title: Remote Access
docs.text: Remote access allows the Mydia mobile app to connect to your Mydia instance from anywhere, even when your server is behind NAT or a firewall.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Mydia uses libp2p for decentralized peer-to-peer connectivity:

  1. Discovery: Nodes find each other via mDNS (local network) and Kademlia DHT (internet)
  2. Transport: Connections are established over TCP or QUIC, secured with Noise encryption
  3. Media: Media streams (HLS) are served over the libp2p connection via a local proxy in the client

This approach provides: - Decentralized: No central relay dependency for connectivity - NAT Traversal: Built-in hole punching and relay capabilities - Performance: Direct peer-to-peer connections when possible - Reliability: Multiple transport options and automatic fallback

docs.title: Enable Remote Access
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Settings > Remote Access in the Mydia web interface
  2. Toggle Enable Remote Access
  3. Your instance will start the libp2p server and announce itself

docs.title: Direct URLs
docs.text: Direct URLs are automatically detected from your instance's network configuration: - Local IP addresses (e.g., https://192.168.1.100:4443) - Public hostname (if configured) - Custom domain (if configured)

docs.title: Encryption
docs.text:
All communication is encrypted end-to-end using the Noise protocol:

  • Transport: All libp2p connections use Noise encryption
  • Authentication: Peers authenticate via Ed25519 keys
  • Forward Secrecy: Fresh ephemeral keys for each connection

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
• Initial pairing uses claim codes (QR code or 6-digit code)
  • Subsequent connections use device tokens with key exchange
  • Each session establishes fresh encryption keys

docs.title: Certificate Verification
docs.text: For direct HTTPS connections, the app verifies the server's TLS certificate fingerprint against the fingerprint stored during pairing, preventing man-in-the-middle attacks.

docs.title: Libp2p Components
docs.text:
The libp2p implementation is shared between backend and frontend:

  • Core (Rust): native/mydia_p2p_core - shared networking logic
  • Backend (Elixir): Wrapped via Rustler NIF (Mydia.Libp2p)
  • Frontend (Flutter): Wrapped via flutter_rust_bridge

docs.title: Protocols Used
docs.text: Protocol Purpose mDNS Local network discovery Kademlia DHT Internet-wide peer discovery TCP/QUIC Transport layer Noise Encryption and authentication

docs.title: Instance Registration
docs.text: When remote access is enabled, your Mydia instance: 1. Starts the libp2p server 2. Announces itself via mDNS and DHT 3. Listens for incoming peer connections 4. Handles connection requests from paired devices

docs.title: Client Connection
docs.text: When the app connects: 1. Discovers the instance via mDNS or DHT lookup 2. Establishes libp2p connection (TCP or QUIC) 3. Completes Noise handshake for authentication 4. Routes API and media requests over the secure connection

docs.title: App won't connect
docs.text:
1. Check remote access is enabled on your Mydia instance
  2. Verify libp2p server is running - check logs for startup messages
  3. Check claim code - codes expire after 5 minutes

docs.title: Slow performance
docs.text:
1. Check connection type - DHT discovery may take longer than mDNS
  2. Network issues - try from different network to isolate
  3. Firewall rules - ensure UDP ports are open for QUIC

docs.title: Connection drops
docs.text:
The libp2p stack handles reconnection automatically:

  1. Transient failures - automatic retry with backoff
  2. Network change - reconnection after network switch
  3. Long disconnects - may require re-pairing

docs.title: Connection Manager API
docs.text: See player/lib/core/connection/README.md for Flutter implementation details.

docs.title: Adding Media
docs.text: Mydia provides multiple ways to add media to your libraries.

docs.title: Search and Add
docs.text:
The primary way to add media is through the search interface:

  1. Click Search in the navigation
  2. Enter the movie or TV show title
  3. Select the correct result from the search results
  4. Choose a quality profile
  5. Click Add to Library

Mydia will automatically search for releases and download them based on your quality profile settings.

docs.title: Import Existing Media
docs.text:
If you have existing media files, Mydia can import them during library scanning:

  1. Place your media files in the library directory
  2. Trigger a library scan (or wait for automatic scan)
  3. Mydia will match files to metadata and import them

docs.title: File Naming
docs.text:
For best results, use standard naming conventions:

Movies: 

Movie Title (Year)/Movie Title (Year).mkv

TV Shows: 

Show Title (Year)/Season 01/Show Title - S01E01 - Episode Title.mkv

docs.title: Manual Search
docs.text:
For manual control over downloads:

  1. Navigate to the media item
  2. Click Manual Search
  3. Browse available releases
  4. Select and download your preferred release

docs.title: Requests (Multi-User)
docs.text:
Guest users can request media:

  1. Guest searches for media
  2. Guest clicks Request
  3. Admin receives notification
  4. Admin approves or denies request
  5. If approved, media is added and download begins

docs.title: Import Wizard
docs.text:
For bulk imports, use the Import Wizard:

  1. Navigate to Import
  2. Select files or directories
  3. Review matched metadata
  4. Confirm import

docs.title: Managing Libraries
docs.text: Libraries are the core of Mydia's media organization system. Each library represents a collection of media files in a specific directory.

docs.title: Library Types
docs.text:
Type Description Features Movies Feature films Full metadata, downloads, quality profiles Series TV shows with seasons/episodes Episode tracking, air dates, season monitoring Mixed Combined movies and TV shows Both movie and series features Music Music collections File scanning only (experimental) Books E-books and audiobooks File scanning only (experimental) Adult Adult content File scanning only (experimental)

Experimental Library Types

Music, Books, and Adult libraries are highly experimental with minimal functionality. They support basic library scanning and browsing only - no metadata fetching, download automation, or quality profiles.

docs.title: User Management
docs.text: Mydia includes a built-in multi-user system with role-based access control.

docs.title: User Roles
docs.text: Role Permissions Admin Full access: media management, downloads, configuration, request approval Guest Browse library, submit requests for admin approval

docs.title: First User Setup
docs.text:
When you first access Mydia:

  1. You're guided through creating the initial admin user
  2. Choose to set a custom password or generate a secure random one
  3. After creation, you're automatically logged in

docs.title: Local Authentication
docs.text: By default, Mydia uses local username/password authentication.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: LOCAL_AUTH_ENABLED=true

docs.title: Creating Users
docs.text:
Admins can create users through the Admin UI:

  1. Navigate to Admin > Users
  2. Click Add User
  3. Enter username, email, and password
  4. Select role (admin or guest)
  5. Save

docs.title: OIDC/SSO Authentication
docs.text: Mydia supports OpenID Connect (OIDC) for single sign-on integration.

docs.title: Supported Providers
docs.text:
• Keycloak
  • Authelia
  • Auth0
  • Okta
  • Azure AD
  • Google
  • Any OIDC-compliant provider

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
OIDC_ENABLED=true
OIDC_DISCOVERY_DOCUMENT_URI=https://your-provider/.well-known/openid-configuration
OIDC_CLIENT_ID=mydia
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
OIDC_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:4000/auth/oidc/callback
OIDC_SCOPES=openid profile email

docs.title: Auto-Promotion
docs.text: The first user to log in via OIDC is automatically promoted to admin role. Subsequent OIDC users are assigned guest role by default.

docs.title: Provider Configuration
docs.text:
Mydia uses standard OAuth2 authentication with minimal provider configuration:

  • Set client_id, client_secret, and redirect_uris in your provider
  • No need to configure token endpoint auth methods or response modes

docs.title: Request System
docs.text:
Guest users can request media:

  1. Guest searches for a movie or TV show
  2. Guest clicks Request on the search result
  3. Admin receives notification of the request
  4. Admin reviews and approves or denies
  5. If approved, media is added to library and download begins
  6. Guest is notified of the decision

docs.title: Managing Requests
docs.text:
Admins can view and manage requests:

  1. Navigate to Admin > Requests
  2. View pending requests
  3. Approve or deny each request
  4. Optionally add a message

docs.title: Disabling Authentication
docs.text:
Security Warning

Disabling authentication is not recommended for production deployments.

For local/testing environments, you can disable local auth when using OIDC:

LOCAL_AUTH_ENABLED=false
OIDC_ENABLED=true
